text:
mira: FYI I spun up a focused canary (kv-longctx-magnet70-int8) to validate int8 packing + rope-scaling changes from PR#4921. Quick smoke reveals output drift after ~16384 tokens.
jon: is it a content shift or hallucination/regression?
mira: content shift + repeated span. Up to token ~16384 outputs match fp16 reference, immediately after we start seeing a 1-token left-shift in attention targets and occasional 2-token repeats.
sasha: left-shift how? example diff please.
mira: fp16: "...she reached the summit before dawn and..."  int8: "...she reached the summit before dawn she reached the summit before..."  so prefix loops.
tao: sounds like an index wrap or off-by-one when stitching prefill and streaming KV writes. Our int8 pack reduces per-key stride and we moved to byte-level packing in that PR. Could be packing offset floor/ceil mismatch.
mira: logging shows repeated: "kvcache_write: expected_byte_offset=65536 actual=65535, corrective_adjust=1" around the fail point.
jon: that 65536 is very round; what's the shard size and stride here?
mira: shard_size_bytes=8192, stride_tokens=2048 for this model config, so at token boundary 8k*2 we hit math that ends up exactly hitting a multiple of 64 bytes on the fp16 path and off-by-one on packed path.
sasha: interesting: earlier we saw many regressions keyed to 4096 multiples, this one is 8192/16384 multiples. maybe the new layernorm fused kernel changed prefill chunking.
tao: hypothesis: RoPE phase scaling uses float32 accumulation on fp16 path but we quantize phase factors for int8 ahead of packing. When we apply scale_to_context we round-phase -> quantize -> pack; rounding pushes some phase indices across the boundary by +-1 bit, which when interpreted as an index leads to a shift.
mira: reproduced locally with a tiny prompt by forcing prefill size:

```
python -m repro.longrun \
  --model magnet70b-int8 \
  --prompt tests/long_prompts/long_paragraph_18k.txt \
  --force-prefill 16384 \
  --quant-mode packed_byte8 \
  --seed 7
```

mira: fingerprint tool output at boundary: "shard4: ref=0x9a4f11 canary=0x9a4f10" 1 difference.
jon: single bit / byte diff then. that matches off-by-one packing hypothesis.
sasha: any env signal? ops-bot, fleets?
ops-bot: p4d-eu nodes have driver 535.65, a100-us-east 535.86. No kernel upgrade in the last 2 weeks.
tao: okay ignore drivers for now. plan: add an optional path that computes kvcache offsets in 64-bit integers and also emits pre-pack validation hashes. if pre-pack hashes match fp16, then packing is safe, otherwise abort and log.
mira: can we do a cheap fallback to unpacked int8 for the affected shard indices so we can keep canary running while we iterate?
tao: yes, implement per-shard fallback. Also add a unit test that constructs synthetic keys that align to byte boundaries and asserts pack/unpack roundtrip equality.
jon: do we have eval metrics? how bad is quality?
mira: on longforms-10k set: fp16 PPL ~7.8, int8 pre-fix PPL ~7.9; after boundary fp16 still ~7.8, int8 jumps to 11.2. BLEU-style ngram F1 drops ~5 pts.
sasha: not acceptable. prioritize fix.
tao: I'll open branch kv-int8-pack-safeguard and push a debug build to canary. also adding diagnostic env var KV_PACK_DEBUG=1 to enable pre-pack fingerprinting.
mira: thanks. I uploaded the failing prompt + the token-alignment diff to the ticket. tagging @tao @jon.
jon: CI? dev-ci-bot, canary trigger?
dev-ci-bot: build pipeline started for branch/kv-int8-pack-safeguard. unit tests queued.
tao: pushed initial patch with 64-bit offset comp and pre-pack hash. kicking canary now.
mira: canary log update: pre-pack hashes show mismatch only for shards 3..5. shards 0..2 match reference.
sasha: partial success. narrower failure surface makes it easier to root cause. maybe a misaligned memcpy for shards >2 introduced by iterator arithmetic.
jon: if we can craft a tiny synthetic unit test that reproduces misalignment for a specific shard index, we can root it down quickly. mira, can you write such a test?
mira: yes, on it. will push to tests/kv/pack_alignment_test.py.
tao: FYI disabling scale_to_context removes mismatch but PPL regresses across the whole eval, so it's not an acceptable workaround.
jon: schedule: if we don't have a stable patch in 4 hours rollback will revert packing optimization in canary and apply safelisted non-packed int8 build.
mira: thanks everyone. logging pinned and retention 48h. will update thread with test PR and canary links. :white_check_mark:
